photos.question: A client is prescribed metronidazole for an infection. Which instruction should the nurse include?
photos.caption:
💊 NCLEX PRACTICE QUESTION #280!

🍷 One drink with this antibiotic can make a client very sick. Do you know which rule?

This is a HIGH-YIELD pharmacology question every nursing student should know! 🩺

👇 Comment your answer before checking!

.
.
.
.
.
.
.
.

✅ Correct Answer: B — Avoid alcohol during and after therapy

🧠 Rationale: Metronidazole plus alcohol can cause a disulfiram-like reaction.

Signs include flushing, nausea, vomiting and a fast heart rate.

Avoid alcohol during therapy and for at least 3 days after the last dose.

📚 NCLEX Must-Know: Metronidazole

💊 Drug Class: Nitroimidazole antibiotic and antiprotozoal

❤️ Primary Use: C. diff, anaerobic infections, trichomoniasis, giardia

⚠️ Side Effects:

🔹 Metallic taste

🔹 Nausea

🔹 Dark urine

🔹 Numbness or tingling with long use

🚨 Patient Teaching:

✅ No alcohol, including mouthwash with alcohol

✅ Finish the full course

✅ Report numbness or seizures

💡 NCLEX MEMORY TIP:

Metro + booze = big trouble!

❤️ Follow @ryan__glass for daily NCLEX practice questions!

photos.question: Which finding should the nurse expect in a client with a deep vein thrombosis (DVT) of the left leg?
photos.caption:
💊 NCLEX PRACTICE QUESTION #281!

🦵 One leg is swollen and warm after surgery. What are you looking at?

This is a HIGH-YIELD cardiovascular question every nursing student should know! 🩺

👇 Comment your answer before checking!

.
.
.
.
.
.
.
.

✅ Correct Answer: A — Swelling and warmth of the left calf

🧠 Rationale: A DVT blocks venous return in one leg.

Expect swelling, warmth, redness and calf pain on that side.

A cool, pale, pulseless leg points to an arterial problem instead.

📚 NCLEX Must-Know: Deep Vein Thrombosis

❤️ Risk Factors: Surgery, bed rest, long travel, pregnancy, estrogen, smoking

⚠️ Signs:

🔹 Swelling of one leg

🔹 Warmth and redness

🔹 Calf pain or tenderness

🚨 Nursing Actions:

✅ Do not massage the leg

✅ Give anticoagulants as prescribed

✅ Early ambulation to prevent DVT

✅ SCDs only on the unaffected leg

🚑 Emergency: Sudden chest pain and shortness of breath may mean a PE. Call the rapid response team.

💡 NCLEX MEMORY TIP:

Never rub a clot!

❤️ Follow @ryan__glass for daily NCLEX practice questions!

#NCLEX #NursingSchool #NCLEXPrep #Cardiac #DVT #MedSurg #NursingTips #NursingStudent #FutureRN #NursingEducation

photos.question: A client exposed to a faulty home heater has a headache and confusion. SpO2 is 99%. What should the nurse do first?
photos.caption:
💊 NCLEX PRACTICE QUESTION #282!

🔥 The pulse ox reads 99%, but this client is in danger. Do you know why?

This is a HIGH-YIELD respiratory question every nursing student should know! 🩺

👇 Comment your answer before checking!

.
.
.
.
.
.
.
.

✅ Correct Answer: C — Give 100% oxygen by nonrebreather mask

🧠 Rationale: Carbon monoxide binds hemoglobin much more tightly than oxygen.

Pulse oximetry cannot tell the difference, so SpO2 looks falsely normal.

100% oxygen speeds removal of carbon monoxide from the blood.

📚 NCLEX Must-Know: Carbon Monoxide Poisoning

⚠️ Signs:

🔹 Headache

🔹 Dizziness and confusion

🔹 Nausea

🔹 Cherry red skin (late sign)

🚨 Nursing Actions:

✅ Give 100% O2 by nonrebreather

✅ Check carboxyhemoglobin level

✅ Monitor neuro status

✅ Hyperbaric oxygen if severe

🏠 Patient Teaching:

✅ Install CO detectors at home

✅ Have heaters checked yearly

💡 NCLEX MEMORY TIP:

CO fools the pulse ox. Trust the symptoms!

❤️ Follow @ryan__glass for daily NCLEX practice questions!

#NCLEX #NursingSchool #NCLEXPrep #Respiratory #CarbonMonoxide #EmergencyNursing #ERNurse #NursingStudent #FutureRN #NursingEducation

photos.question: At 20 weeks of pregnancy, where should the nurse expect to palpate the fundus?
photos.caption:
💊 NCLEX PRACTICE QUESTION #283!

🤰 Halfway there! Where should the fundus be at 20 weeks?

This is a HIGH-YIELD maternity question every nursing student should know! 🩺

👇 Comment your answer before checking!

.
.
.
.
.
.
.
.

✅ Correct Answer: B — At the umbilicus

🧠 Rationale: At 20 weeks the fundus is usually at the level of the umbilicus.

From 20 to about 36 weeks, fundal height in cm roughly matches the weeks of pregnancy.

📚 NCLEX Must-Know: Fundal Height

📏 Landmarks:

🔹 12 weeks: just above the symphysis pubis

🔹 20 weeks: at the umbilicus

🔹 36 weeks: near the xiphoid process

🚨 Nursing Actions:

✅ Client voids before measuring

✅ Measure from symphysis to top of fundus

✅ Report a size 3 cm or more off dates

💡 NCLEX MEMORY TIP:

20 weeks, 20 cm, belly button!

❤️ Follow @ryan__glass for daily NCLEX practice questions!

photos.question: A client in an acute manic episode will not sit down for meals. Which intervention is best?
photos.caption:
💊 NCLEX PRACTICE QUESTION #284!

🏃 This client is too busy to sit down and eat. What do you do?

This is a HIGH-YIELD mental health question every nursing student should know! 🩺

👇 Comment your answer before checking!

.
.
.
.
.
.
.
.

✅ Correct Answer: A — Offer high-calorie finger foods

🧠 Rationale: Clients in mania burn a lot of energy and have trouble sitting still.

High-calorie, high-protein finger foods can be eaten on the go.

Forcing the client to sit can increase agitation.

📚 NCLEX Must-Know: Mania

⚠️ Signs:

🔹 Little need for sleep

🔹 Racing thoughts and fast speech

🔹 Grandiosity

🔹 Constant movement

🚨 Nursing Actions:

✅ Low-stimulation environment

✅ Finger foods and fluids often

✅ Short, clear statements

✅ Monitor weight and sleep

💊 Common Meds: Lithium, valproate, atypical antipsychotics

💡 NCLEX MEMORY TIP:

Mania on the move? Food that moves too!

❤️ Follow @ryan__glass for daily NCLEX practice questions!

photos.question: The nurse is teaching a client who uses oxygen at home. Which instruction is correct?
photos.caption:
💊 NCLEX PRACTICE QUESTION #285!

🕯️ Home oxygen saves lives, but one mistake can start a fire. Which rule is right?

This is a HIGH-YIELD safety question every nursing student should know! 🩺

👇 Comment your answer before checking!

.
.
.
.
.
.
.
.

✅ Correct Answer: D — Keep the oxygen away from open flames

🧠 Rationale: Oxygen is not flammable, but it makes fire burn hotter and faster.

No smoking, candles, gas stoves or open flames near oxygen.

Use water-based products, not petroleum jelly.

📚 NCLEX Must-Know: Home Oxygen Safety

🚨 Patient Teaching:

✅ Post No Smoking signs

✅ Keep away from heat sources

✅ Use water-based lip and nose products

✅ Do not change the flow rate without an order

⚠️ Hazards:

🔹 Cigarettes and candles

🔹 Gas stoves and fireplaces

🔹 Petroleum or oil-based products

🚑 Emergency: Shut off oxygen and leave the room if a fire starts.

💡 NCLEX MEMORY TIP:

O2 and fire never share a room!

photos.question: A newborn has not passed meconium 48 hours after birth and has a distended abdomen. What should the nurse suspect?
photos.caption:
💊 NCLEX PRACTICE QUESTION #286!

👶 48 hours and still no first stool. What could this be?

This is a HIGH-YIELD pediatric question every nursing student should know! 🩺

👇 Comment your answer before checking!

.
.
.
.
.
.
.
.

✅ Correct Answer: C — Hirschsprung disease

🧠 Rationale: Hirschsprung disease means part of the colon has no nerve cells.

Stool cannot move through, so meconium is delayed and the belly distends.

Most newborns pass meconium within 24 to 48 hours.

📚 NCLEX Must-Know: Hirschsprung Disease

⚠️ Signs:

🔹 No meconium in 24 to 48 hours

🔹 Abdominal distention

🔹 Bilious vomiting

🔹 Ribbon-like, foul stools in older kids

🔬 Diagnosis: Rectal biopsy showing no ganglion cells

🚨 Nursing Actions:

✅ Measure abdominal girth

✅ Report fever or explosive diarrhea

✅ Prepare family for surgery

💡 NCLEX MEMORY TIP:

No nerves, no movement!
